# Proposal: Implementation Accelerator for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026
**Decision requested by:** 15 December 2026

---

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. The Client is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in Germany and the United States. Its use of AI is at three stages:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

In June 2026 an internal audit finding recorded that Tamarack has no inventory of AI systems. Your stated objective is clear: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." The EU AI Act and GDPR are the regulatory drivers. ISO/IEC 42001 work is expected to begin next year, although the start date is not yet fixed.

Three constraints shape the work:

- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.
- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

Tamarack already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system and an ISO 9001 quality management system. This is a significant advantage. ISO/IEC 42001 shares the harmonized management system structure used by both standards. Tamarack's AI Management System (AIMS) should therefore extend what already works rather than create a parallel bureaucracy. Every artifact in this proposal names the existing system it attaches to.

## 2. Why an Intensive AIMS Foundation Build Fits Now

**Decision timeline.** A decision by 15 December 2026 allows the Implementation Accelerator to run in a five-day window in January 2027. This window is proposed and subject to confirmation. It leaves the Client most of Q1 2027 to adopt artifacts through its own governance, consult the works council and apply controls to the visual inspection pilot before the Q2 2027 production go-live. Delaying the foundation work would compress consultation and adoption into the weeks immediately before go-live.

**Certification target.** The Accelerator structures artifacts for future ISO/IEC 42001 conformity work. Starting now means that when the Client fixes its 42001 start date, it begins from a working foundation and not a blank page. The outcome is readiness. This proposal does not promise certification or any audit result.

**Audit finding.** The inventory built on Day 2 responds directly to the June 2026 finding. It also gives the internal auditors a defined artifact to test.

**Budget fit.** The Implementation Accelerator is priced at US$25,000, within the US$80,000 approved for this fiscal year.

**Regulatory orientation.** The points below are orientation only and do not constitute legal advice.

- **Customer service chatbot.** EU AI Act transparency obligations for systems that interact with people are likely relevant. The chatbot also processes customer personal data under GDPR, and the EU data residency constraint becomes a design requirement in the inventory and vendor policy. *Confirm with external counsel.*
- **Visual inspection.** Classification under the EU AI Act depends on facts not yet known, including the system's role in product quality and safety. Classification will be worked through on Day 2. *Confirm with external counsel.*
- **Works council.** Systems that are capable of monitoring employee behaviour or performance may trigger German co-determination rights. The visual inspection pilot should be assessed for this before production use. *Confirm with external counsel.*
- **Sales forecasting.** This system is planned rather than deployed. It enters the inventory now so that it is governed from design onward.

## 3. The Five-Day Build Spine, Tailored to Tamarack

The sequence respects two dependencies. The charter precedes policies, and the inventory precedes the risk register.

| Day | Build Focus | Tamarack Tailoring | Attachment Point |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Governance charter and roles | Decision rights across Legal, Security, Quality, Data and plant operations. Defines the works council consultation trigger. Executive checkpoint. | ISO 9001 management review; ISMS governance forum |
| 2 | AI system inventory and classification | Chatbot, visual inspection pilot and sales forecasting entered as first records. Records EU AI Act orientation and data residency fields for each system. | ISO/IEC 27001 asset inventory (Annex A 5.9) |
| 3 | Risk and impact assessment plus risk register | Risk statements seeded from the three use cases and the audit finding, as drafts for Client validation. Includes an impact assessment of the visual inspection pilot on production staff. | ISMS risk assessment methodology (Clause 6.1.2); QMS risk-based thinking |
| 4 | Core policies and operating procedures | Covers acceptable use, AI lifecycle governance, vendor and supplier governance, incident response and change management. | ISO 9001 design and development (8.3) and control of changes (8.5.6); ISMS supplier relationships (Annex A 5.19) and incident management (Annex A 5.24) |
| 5 | Evidence model, implementation priorities and executive readout | Evidence index mapped to assurance questions the internal auditors can test. 90-day priorities anchored to the Q2 2027 go-live. Executive checkpoint. | ISO 9001 internal audit (9.2) and documented information (7.5) |

The build draws on two open frameworks. The GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) structures the governance, risk and compliance artifacts. The Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) structures the operational discipline behind them. The Day 5 executive readout draws on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

## 4. Artifacts Tamarack Owns at Close

1. AI Governance Charter, covering purpose, scope, roles, decision rights and meeting cadence.
2. Roles and Decision Rights Matrix.
3. AI System Inventory and Classification Schema, populated with the three known use cases.
4. AI Risk and Impact Assessment Method.
5. AI Risk Register, with seeded risk statements labeled as drafts for Client validation.
6. Visual Inspection Pre-Production Impact Assessment, in draft, including a works council consultation input pack.
7. AI Acceptable Use Policy.
8. AI Lifecycle Governance Policy.
9. AI Vendor and Supplier Governance Policy, incorporating the EU data residency requirement.
10. AI Incident Response Procedure.
11. AI Change Management Procedure.
12. Evidence Index, mapping each artifact to the assurance question it answers.
13. Prioritized 90-Day Implementation Plan with named owners.
14. Executive Readout.

**Status and storage.** At close, each artifact carries a status of draft or reviewed. Adoption remains a Client act carried out through Tamarack's own governance and works council processes. All artifacts are built and stored in the Client's own document system, so working content stays under Tamarack's control.

## 5. Team Composition Asked of the Client

| Role | Contribution |
|---|---|
| General Counsel (Sponsor) | Charter decision rights, regulatory orientation and executive checkpoints on Days 1 and 5 |
| CISO | ISMS attachment, security controls and vendor and incident procedures |
| Head of Quality | QMS attachment, document control, change management and design controls |
| Head of Data | Inventory, data residency, data quality and the sales forecasting design |
| German plant manager | Visual inspection pilot facts, production impact and works council liaison |
| Two internal auditors | Challenge and testability review of the evidence model |

We recommend that the internal auditors act as reviewers rather than artifact owners. Their independence matters when they later test the AIMS against their own June 2026 finding.

**Open items to confirm before Day 1:**

- The business owner of the customer service chatbot: `Unknown`.
- The business owner of the sales forecasting initiative: `Unknown`.
- Whether a data protection officer should attend: `Unknown`.
- Executive attendees beyond the Sponsor for the Day 1 and Day 5 checkpoints: `Unknown`.

## 6. Guiding Principles

The work is guided by three principles:

- **Slow AI.** Production use of visual inspection waits for governance, not the reverse.
- **Informed Intent.** Each AI system is inventoried with a stated purpose and an accountable owner.
- **Final Liability rests with the Human.** Every decision right in the charter is assigned to a named role, never to a system.

## 7. Logistics and Price

- **Format:** five consecutive working days of live virtual working sessions with structured build time each afternoon.
- **Proposed window:** January 2027, with dates to be confirmed.
- **Price:** US$25,000.
- **Continuation:** options are presented with rationale at the Day 5 readout and are outside the scope of this proposal.

## 8. Next Step

We propose a 30-minute call before 15 December 2026 to cover three items:

1. Confirm the delivery window.
2. Name the open roles listed in Section 5.
3. Agree on the pre-work pack. This includes existing ISMS and QMS procedures, the June 2026 audit finding and the available documentation for the three AI use cases.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
